A1-A2.headline: Carmen Miranda: Queen of Samba and Cinema

pages.text: Carmen Miranda was a Portuguese-born singer, dancer, and movie actress who grew up in Brazil. Fans loved her playful energy and bright hats topped with colorful fruit. Her early samba recordings quickly turned her into Brazil's most famous singing star.

Born in Portugal, Miranda traveled with her family to live in Brazil when she was very young. Her father loved opera and named her Carmen after his favorite musical show. Her mother secretly supported Miranda's singing dreams when she started out.

pages.text: In Brazil, composer Josué de Barros helped Miranda record her first joyful samba song. Soon Carmen Miranda signed top radio contracts and became the country's highest-paid singer. Newspapers gave her lively nicknames celebrating her sparkling voice and bright smile.

pages.text: Carmen Miranda later sailed to New York and became an instant sensation on Broadway stages. Radio host Walter Winchell praised her rhythmic singing across America, boosting ticket sales dramatically. Soon audiences adored her vibrant music and charming stage style.

B1-B2.headline: From Rio Radio Star to Hollywood Icon

pages.text: Known worldwide as the Brazilian Bombshell, Carmen Miranda became an unforgettable singer, dancer, and film star. Before hitting American cinema in vibrant fruit hats, she pioneered samba recordings in Brazil. Her breakthrough records captivated listeners and transformed Brazilian popular music.

Born in northern Portugal before emigrating to Brazil, Miranda grew up surrounded by opera music. When her father opposed theater work, her mother courageously supported her early auditions. Young Carmen soon traded boutique hat design for a bright stage career.

C1-C2.headline: Carmen Miranda Between Samba Roots and Hollywood

pages.text: Celebrated internationally as the Brazilian Bombshell, Carmen Miranda achieved stardom spanning samba radio and Hollywood musicals. Beginning her career designing hats, she soon transformed Brazilian recording history through dazzling vocal charisma. Signature tropical costumes ultimately turned her into an enduring global icon.

Born in rural Portugal shortly before her family migrated to Brazil, Miranda discovered performance early. Despite maternal support amid harsh paternal disapproval, she pursued musical auditions relentlessly. Childhood immersion in European opera blended naturally with vibrant Afro-Brazilian rhythms.

title: Homonationalism, Pinkwashing, and Identity Politics
attribution: Adapted from English Wikipedia contributors; see pinned revision and history. SAGA AI-assisted adaptation under CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikipedia does not endorse SAGA.

pages.text: Homonationalism is an academic concept describing how some nations selectively celebrate queer rights in order to promote nationalism. Activists in France and elsewhere have held public demonstrations against homonationalism during Labour Day marches and political events.
pages.caption: Demonstration against homonationalism during Labour Day 2012 in France by Les Panthères roses [fr]

evidence.articleCaption: Demonstration against homonationalism during Labour Day 2012 in France by Les Panthères roses [fr]

pages.text: Gender studies scholar Jasbir K. Puar first coined the word homonationalism in her influential book on queer politics and Western power. She observed that nationalist stories often paint immigrants from Muslim-majority countries as backward to make Western states look morally superior.

Philosopher Judith Butler expanded the discussion by examining how progressive laws such as same-sex marriage can be framed as proof of national identity. Scholars note that these arguments frequently rise alongside anti-immigrant rhetoric while ignoring prejudice still present inside Western societies.

Closely connected is pinkwashing, sometimes called rainbow-washing, a phrase that emerged informally in the United States. Pinkwashing describes how governments, companies, or institutions use friendly queer slogans to look progressive while distracting critics from other harmful policies.

Sociologist Sara R. Farris later introduced a related idea called femonationalism to analyze similar political strategies around women's rights. Just like homonationalism, femonationalism explores how nationalist movements adopt selected feminist themes to justify anti-immigrant policies.

Homonationalism is an academic framework analyzing how states selectively embrace queer rights to advance nationalist ideologies. Public activism, including Labour Day demonstrations against homonationalism in France, highlights growing debate over how human rights are invoked in national politics.

pages.text: Coined by gender studies scholar Jasbir K. Puar in Terrorist Assemblages, homonationalism examines how Western liberal institutions co-opt certain queer identities. Critics argue such narratives lean on orientalist stereotypes portraying immigrants from Muslim-majority nations as inherently intolerant compared with Western society.

Philosopher Judith Butler deepened this critique, characterizing the pattern as sexual politics where milestones like same-sex marriage reinforce exclusionary national identity. Scholars emphasize that these discourses often pair with anti-immigrant hostility while overlooking ongoing domestic homophobia.

A companion concept known as pinkwashing—or rainbow-washing—emerged in the United States to critique strategic institutional branding. It refers to states or corporations adopting visibly queer-friendly messaging to appear progressive while deflecting scrutiny from unrelated abuses or inequalities.

Building parallel theory, sociologist Sara R. Farris coined femonationalism to describe how nationalist platforms and neoliberal policies enlist feminist language. Like homonationalism, femonationalism scrutinizes how selective rights rhetoric can be mobilized behind anti-immigrant agendas.

Homonationalism designates a critical academic concept examining the selective incorporation of queer acceptance into nationalist political projects. Civic pushback—illustrated by French Labour Day demonstrations against homonationalism—reflects ongoing contention over how rights discourse serves state legitimacy.

A1-A2.headline: Tracking a Drug-Resistant Fungus in Hospitals

pages.text: Candida auris is a rare fungus growing like a yeast that can cause hospital infections. The emergence of Candida auris worried doctors because several strong medicines fail to kill it. Careful cleaning stops this tough fungus from spreading on medical rooms.
pages.caption: Proposed scheme for the emergence of C. auris.

pages.text: Doctors first discovered Candida auris inside an elderly patient's ear in Tokyo before cases appeared elsewhere. Soon hospitals across South Korea, Asia, Europe, and the United States noticed outbreaks. Misidentifying it as milder yeasts sometimes delayed proper treatment early on.

Under microscopes, Candida auris forms smooth whitish-gray yeast colonies and takes its name from Latin for ear. Scientists found the fungus uses an amazing White-Brown epigenetic switch between two states. This biological switching changes how well Candida auris resists stress and skin cleaning.
pages.caption: White-Brown epigenetic switching in Candida auris

evidence.articleCaption: White-Brown epigenetic switching in Candida auris

pages.text: Early history records traced outbreaks back to hospital blood infections in South Korea and Delhi. Investigators learned the exact same fungal strain quietly spread across separate surgical and newborn hospital rooms. Checking stored laboratory specimens showed the germ existed years earlier.

Because bloodstream infections carry dangerous risks for weak patients, hospitals test carefully for this yeast now. Faster lab tools help doctors spot Candida auris quickly instead of confusing its identity. Strict hand hygiene protects long-term care residents everywhere.

B1-B2.headline: Why Candida Auris Worries Global Hospitals

pages.text: Candida auris is a resilient yeast species capable of triggering dangerous bloodstream candidiasis inside hospitals. Its rapid global emergence alarmed physicians because many strains survive multiple standard antifungal drugs. Patients with weakened immunity in long-term care face highest risk.

pages.text: First identified from an ear canal sample in Tokyo, Candida auris subsequently appeared across continents. Outbreaks soon surfaced in South Korea, wider Asia, Europe, and the United States. Routine lab equipment frequently mistook the yeast for common related species.

Growing as smooth grayish yeast colonies, Candida auris derives its scientific name from the Latin word for ear. Crucially, the fungus performs reversible White-Brown epigenetic switching between two cellular states. Switching alters skin survival, stress endurance, and shifting sensitivity to antifungal treatments.

pages.text: Historical microbiology investigations later confirmed early South Korean bloodstream infections had been misidentified years earlier. In Delhi hospitals, investigators discovered identical clonal Candida auris strains infecting patients across separated wards. That finding proved persistent hospital surfaces silently transmitted infections.

A1-A2.headline: What Is the American FairTax Sales Proposal?

pages.text: FairTax is a fixed-rate national sales tax plan introduced repeatedly in the United States Congress. The bill proposes closing the Internal Revenue Service and taxing all new household goods and services at checkout while sending every family a monthly rebate payment.

Economists and lawmakers strongly dispute how the FairTax would shift the overall tax burden across American workers and families. Supporters claim a broader tax base would lower rates on workers, though critics question how fair its economic welfare impact truly is.

pages.text: Moving away from income taxes would also reshape government agencies dramatically during the transition period. Over a hundred thousand Internal Revenue Service workers could lose their federal positions, while supporters estimate multibillion-dollar annual savings from closing that tax bureaucracy.

Backers argue that replacing federal income taxes with a general sales tax would shrink tax filers sharply and simplify paperwork into basic state forms. However, federal watchdogs at the Government Accountability Office warn that high sales taxes could encourage new evasion.

B1-B2.headline: How the FairTax Aims to Replace Federal Income Taxes

pages.text: Introduced annually in the United States Congress, the FairTax proposes abolishing the Internal Revenue Service and repealing federal income tax authority. Instead, consumers would pay a fixed national sales tax on new retail purchases while receiving monthly household rebates scaled to family size.

How the FairTax redistributes the tax burden remains fiercely contested among policy scholars. Proponents—citing economic working papers—contend that widening the tax base would create a progressive system with lower effective burdens on workers, while critics dispute its welfare incidence.

Most employees inside the Internal Revenue Service would face job displacement, though the Beacon Hill Institute estimated billions in potential federal administrative budget reductions.

pages.text: Anchored along the right bank of Andalusia's Guadalquivir River, historic Córdoba embodies Spain's rich civilizational crossroads. Stone lanes invite unhurried exploration through sunlit courtyards.

From ancient prehistoric cave camps to consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus's city foundation, Córdoba flourished swiftly under Roman administration. pages.text: Gracefully lining Andalusia's Guadalquivir riverbed, Córdoba stands as a monumental palimpsest of Iberian cultural history. Evolving successively through Roman provincial administration, Visigothic monarchy, and Islamic governance, every plaza preserves extraordinary continuity. Sunlit stone arches mirror centuries of intellectual exchange.

Prehistoric Neanderthal traces precede Consul Marcellus's planned Roman foundation, subsequently elevated as capital of Hispania Ulterior. Rebuilt extensively under Augustus after Julius Caesar's punitive siege, classical grandeur crystallized within the towering Roman temple of Córdoba. Classical civic geometry long endured underground.

pages.text: Based in Dharamshala, India, the Central Tibetan Administration serves as Tibet's democratic government-in-exile. Following his escape from Tibet into India, the fourteenth Dalai Lama formally rescinded the earlier agreement with China and restored the traditional Kashag governing council in exile.

Worldwide Tibetan diaspora communities and refugees actively sustain the Central Tibetan Administration by voting democratically for parliament members and the Sikyong leader while paying voluntary annual financial contributions recorded through the traditional Green Book system.

In exile, the fourteenth Dalai Lama promulgated a formal Constitution of Tibet and served as permanent head of state before later rejecting calls for outright Tibetan independence in favor of sustained autonomy and institutional continuity.

Operating from its Dharamshala headquarters alongside cultural repositories preserving Tibetan works and archives, the administration supports roughly one hundred thousand Tibetan exiles in India. Its public services span schools, healthcare clinics, cultural preservation, and local economic development.

A1-A2.headline: Sea Walls and Republic History in Dubrovnik

pages.text: Dubrovnik, known historically as Ragusa, shines along Croatia's sunny southern Adriatic Sea coast. Strong stone medieval city walls surround terracotta roofs beside deep clear Mediterranean waters. UNESCO named Dubrovnik's dramatic Old City a cherished World Heritage treasure.

According to old legends, fleeing Roman neighbors founded Ragusa upon a rocky seaside island ages ago. Excavations uncovered thick old Byzantine walls and buried church stones showing bustling medieval seaside towns existed early. Sea captains traded across calm bays safely.

B1-B2.headline: How the Free Republic of Ragusa Built Dubrovnik

pages.text: Clinging to Croatia's limestone Adriatic coast, Dubrovnik—historically Ragusa—ranks among Europe's best-preserved medieval walled seaports. Maritime trade fueled proud self-rule for centuries under Byzantine protection and Venetian sovereignty. UNESCO honored the entire Old City for breathtaking stone fortifications.

Old chronicles record refugees from ruined Epidaurum settling Ragusa's rocky sea island near Illyrian tribes. Modern excavations confirmed thick early walls and an ancient Byzantine basilica anchored prosperous medieval coastal trade. Maritime crossroads drew diverse sailors smoothly.

C1-C2.headline: Maritime Diplomacy and Stone Heritage of Dubrovnik

pages.text: Crowning southern Dalmatia's jagged Adriatic cliffs, Dubrovnik—historically celebrated as Ragusa—exemplifies resilient medieval maritime urbanism. Sustained through centuries of nuanced diplomacy linking Byzantine protectors and Venetian suzerainty, its monumental defenses merited UNESCO World Heritage status. Red-tiled bastions still confront gleaming azure seas.

Byzantine chronicles attribute Ragusa's origins to Epidaurum refugees colonizing a coastal islet beside Illyrian settlements. Archaeological excavations subsequently unearthed an eighth-century Byzantine basilica alongside fortified walls attesting to vigorous early commerce. Maritime trade quickly knitted inland Dalmatian communities together.

pages.text: Evolving into an aristocratic Republic of Ragusa, shrewd statesmen balanced formal Ottoman tribute against unrivaled Adriatic merchant autonomy. Civic engineering flourished memorably through sanitary Lazareti complexes and Big Onofrio's ornate monumental fountain. Ragusa's merchant thalassocracy directly rivaled Italy's proudest maritime republics.

Sustaining diplomatic neutrality unlocked lucrative Mediterranean spice corridors while medieval hinterland records attest multicultural Albanian and Slavic exchange. Despite devastating seventeenth-century earthquakes, civic solidarity meticulously restored grand limestone boulevards cleanly. Centuries of mercantile governance forged an extraordinary civic monument.
